verdict_reason: Paging cases exercise the right behaviour, but one cannot fail for its titled claim (page-offset numbering), one over-claims 'every paging link', and the page size is redeclared beside pagination.js's export.

todos.issue: The case titled 'Should number the rows of the page after the first from where that page starts' (lines 205-216) asserts only that page 2's one row gets the bare field name. The first row of any page always gets the bare name (view-model.js:11, index === 0), so nothing here sees the page offset: removing 'from +' from idPrefixFor leaves the test green. The title claims numbering from the page start; the assertion proves only the first-row rule.
todos.fix: Must: the test goes red if row numbering on a later page ignores the page offset, and its title states exactly what it asserts. One way: build ADDRESSES_A_PAGE + 2 records, open page 2, and assert the idPrefixes equal [fieldName, `${fieldName}-10`].

todos.issue: 'Should carry the ticked address through every paging link' (lines 196-203) loops over pagination.items only. The next link (pagination.next.href) is a paging link too and is never checked, so the title over-claims; a regression that dropped 'selected' from the previous/next hrefs would stay green.
todos.fix: Must: the assertions cover every link the title names (numbered items and the previous/next link present on that page), or the title names only the numbered links. One way: collect [...items.map(i => i.href), pagination.next.href] and assert each contains 'selected=record-3'.

todos.issue: Line 133 declares its own 'const ADDRESSES_A_PAGE = 8', the same name pagination.js:4 already exports, and the sibling paging-test-support.js:6 imports that export. Two test-support modules of one feature take the page size from different homes under one name, so a change to the page size updates one suite and not the other.
todos.fix: Must: the picker's test support has one source for the page size, used by both test-support.js and paging-test-support.js. One way: import ADDRESSES_A_PAGE from './pagination.js' here and delete the local declaration (or, if the suites must pin 8 independently, give the pinned literal its own name in one shared place and use it in both).

todos.issue: pageOfAddresses(count) (line 138) returns 'count' numbered address records, not a page: every call but one passes OVER_A_PAGE (lines 153, 169, 198, 210), i.e. more than a page holds, so the name mispredicts what it returns.
todos.fix: Must: the helper's name says it returns that many numbered address records, whatever the count. One way: rename to numberedAddresses(count) at the declaration and all four call sites.

todos.issue: Literals used by one function sit at module scope: JOURNEY_ID and GIVEN_SLUG (lines 63-64) are used only inside viewModelBoundFor, and SECOND_PAGE and LAST_OF_OVER_A_PAGE (lines 135-136) only inside pagingCases. The house rule keeps a literal used by one function in that function.
todos.fix: Must: each literal used by a single function lives inside that function; module scope keeps only values the module shares. One way: move JOURNEY_ID and GIVEN_SLUG into viewModelBoundFor, and SECOND_PAGE and LAST_OF_OVER_A_PAGE into pagingCases.
